chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) stood upon As-Safa and said: 'O Clan of Hashim! O Clan of Abdul Muttalib! I am the Messenger of Allah to you, and I am compassionate towards you, and for me is my deed, and for every man among you is his deed. Do not say that Muhammad is from us and so we shall enter where he enters, so no, by Allah! My friends are not from you, nor from the others, O Clan of Abdul Muttalib, except the pious ones. So I will not recognize you on the Day of Resurrection; you will come carrying the world upon your backs, while the people come carrying the Hereafter. So I have made my excuse to you regarding what is between me and you, and regarding what is between me and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, concerning you.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say to his clan on As-Safa regarding their relationship to his prophethood and the Hereafter?
ai.summary: This narration, recorded in Al-Kafi, highlights the Prophet's declaration of 'I'dhar' (clearing himself of responsibility) to his closest kin, emphasizing that noble lineage does not guarantee salvation without individual piety. It underscores the Shia concept that the Prophet's intercession is limited to the 'Awliya' (the pious), distinguishing between blood relation and spiritual affinity. The warning that the unrighteous will carry the 'weight of the world' illustrates the burden of worldly attachments that hinder entry into the Hereafter.
